interval_head: The interval must stay constant, T* ~ p^0: window failures need six faults, as many as the in-round failures that set the code's floor (six-fault ties; section 4), so the window penalty has the order of the floor and the interval keeping the error within a fixed factor of it is the same at every p
interval_text: The interval must stay constant, T* ~ p^0: window failures need six faults, as many as the in-round failures that set the code's floor (six-fault ties; section 4), so the window penalty has the order of the floor and the interval keeping the error within a fixed factor of it is the same at every p. Lower bound: outside the outer-check gadgets every fault acts on one Carbon block (checked on executed paths), a block then needs 4 faults to carry an undetected inner logical error through a window whatever rounds its weight-6 checks run in (exact integer programming, windows of T = 2, 4, 8 rounds, 276 paths, X and Z bases, every logical class proved; scripts/inner_window_distance.py), and no logical operator of the code lies on fewer than three blocks: such faults need 12 to leave an undetected logical error, inside a window as in one round, and a most-likely-error decoder fails only with at least 6; with the outer-check gadgets, the whole circuit's fault distance is at least 11 on every path of 7 kinds (non-adaptive extraction over the simulated 8 rounds after preparation, X basis (Z checks last); non-adaptive extraction over the simulated 8 rounds after preparation, Z basis (Z checks last); every path of the escalating and periodic rules over 8 rounds (each weight-6 part optional, an outer-check part in every round), X basis (Z checks last); a periodic window of 16 rounds (push 8), X basis (Z checks last); a periodic window of 8 rounds, X basis (Z checks last); two periodic windows of 4 rounds, X basis (Z checks last); four periodic windows of 2 rounds, X basis (Z checks last); decomposition, section 4), so failures need 6 faults with the gadgets too, in a window as in a round. Upper bound: window failures with six faults exist, constructed directly (two silent errors in one window; analysis/window_failures.py). Measured where the estimates are data-driven, for the escalating rule (ambiguous events, full measurement forced every T rounds): the error depends on the forced interval as T^E with E = -0.01 [-0.15, 0.17] at p = 0.004, 0.00 [-0.09, 0.11] at p = 0.003, 0.02 [-0.13, 0.16] at p = 0.0025 (T = 2 to 8). At these noise levels escalations measure the full syndrome in 69 %, 52 %, 41 % of the rounds without any forcing, so windows rarely reach the forced interval; escalations grow rarer as p falls (below), so the forced interval increasingly bounds the windows, and there the six-fault window failures set the interval. Without forced full measurements a window closes at the next escalation (ambiguous change or fired flag); measured by direct path sampling at every p, escalations occur in 51 % of the rounds at p = 0.003, 12 % of the rounds at p = 0.001, 0.92 % of the rounds at p = 0.0001, falling as p^1.11 below 1e-3: unforced windows last about 1/p rounds, as under the 1/p unmasking rule. Order of the failure probability in the number of faults over the observed strata (exponent in p it implies at the strata's mean fault density): full 5.84 [5.38, 6.26] at p = 3.8e-03, T = 2 6.02 [5.56, 6.43] at p = 3.8e-03, T = 4 5.95 [5.48, 6.38] at p = 3.8e-03, T = 8 5.97 [5.47, 6.44] at p = 3.8e-03. Largest interval in the observed range keeping the error within 1.5x of full extraction: T* >= 8 at p = 0.004, T* >= 8 at p = 0.003, T* >= 8 at p = 0.0025. The 1/p unmasking rule of arXiv:2502.14835 (T = 10 at p = 1e-3, proportional to 1/p) inside the observed T range: error relative to full extraction 1.05 at p = 0.004 (T = 2.5), 1.00 at p = 0.003 (T = 3.3), 1.02 at p = 0.0025 (T = 4.0). Measured with windows that always last the forced interval (periodic family: outer checks only every T rounds, weight-6 checks on events and at the window ends, no escalation - the windows the escalating rules approach as escalations grow rare at low p): error relative to full extraction T = 2: 0.72 [0.58, 0.86] at p = 0.004, 0.76 [0.67, 0.89] at p = 0.003, 0.81 [0.65, 0.97] at p = 0.0025; T = 4: 0.65 [0.57, 0.82] at p = 0.004, 0.65 [0.58, 0.79] at p = 0.003, 0.69 [0.54, 0.87] at p = 0.0025; T = 8: 0.64 [0.53, 0.75] at p = 0.004, 0.74 [0.63, 0.87] at p = 0.003, 0.82 [0.64, 1.02] at p = 0.0025; T = 16: 0.98 [0.80, 1.10] at p = 0.004, 1.07 [0.96, 1.20] at p = 0.003, 1.18 [0.95, 1.37] at p = 0.0025; it depends on the interval as T^E, E = 0.15 [0.07, 0.21] at p = 0.004, 0.17 [0.11, 0.23] at p = 0.003, 0.18 [0.07, 0.26] at p = 0.0025, 0.18 [0.02, 0.31] at p = 0.002 (T = 2 to 16), with no measured dependence on p (dE/d ln p = -0.05 [-0.26, 0.21] over p = 0.004, 0.003, 0.0025, 0.002); per round of window, relative to full extraction, R = a + c (T - 1) with c = 0.022 [0.011, 0.027] at p = 0.004, 0.026 [0.017, 0.035] at p = 0.003, 0.031 [0.015, 0.043] at p = 0.0025; the largest periodic interval keeping the error within 1.5x of full extraction: T* >= 16 at p = 0.004, T* >= 16 at p = 0.003, T* >= 16 at p = 0.0025. Below the data-driven p the ratios come from the order-6 models (labelled extrapolated in the table); T* ~ p^0 there rests on the proven equal orders, which make each ratio tend to a constant (a ratio of six-fault coefficients) as p -> 0, not on the extrapolated values. Without forced full measurements windows close only at escalations, whose measured rate (above) makes them last about 1/p rounds. With the largest extra error per round of window the periodic data allow (c <= 0.043, a <= 0.84, 95 %), that is windows of about 8 rounds at p = 0.001: at most 1.2x full extraction; windows of about 109 rounds at p = 0.0001: at most 5.5x full extraction (extrapolated beyond the 16-round windows measured, assuming the per-round penalty does not grow as p falls, as equal orders imply). As p -> 0 the bound grows with the window length, about 1/p (one fault can trigger an escalation, so the escalation rate is of first order in p; measured exponent above): unforced windows give up one power of p - not less, since six-fault window failures exist - while a constant forced interval keeps the floor's exponent.

tqrb_fig13_text: Under uniform noise our values are about a third of Fig. 13's. The paper's own Fig. 12, the same non-adaptive benchmark under the same noise model and decoder (6 random Cliffords and the inverse), lies as far below Fig. 13: the power law through its γ = 0 markers (slope 2.92) gives 1.41e-04 per Clifford at p = 1e-3, p_L = 9.84e-04 over seven Cliffords, while Fig. 13's non-adaptive p_L(m = 7) is 3.61e-03, 3.2-3.7x more (8 or 7 Cliffords, whether or not m counts the inverse). The definitions cannot account for it: Fig. 12's error per Clifford includes the preparation and measurement share and can only exceed Fig. 13's fitted one for the same data. At p = 5e-4 the factor is 3.0-3.4x (Fig. 12's line extended below its lowest point). Our non-adaptive p_L(m = 7) at p = 1e-3 is 1.13e-03 ± 1.8e-04: 1.14x the value implied by Fig. 12 and 0.31x Fig. 13's; at p = 5e-4 1.54e-04 ± 8.7e-06, 1.18x and 0.35x. Section 1.7 reproduces Fig. 12 directly: without postselection ours / paper = 0.80-0.94 at its three points. The factor of about three between ours and Fig. 13 is therefore one between the paper's two simulations of the same protocol; the smaller differences from Fig. 12 itself are those of section 1.7. Under our Helios-like model (section 1.4) scaled so that its two-qubit error equals p, the same benchmark reproduces Fig. 13 instead: p = 1e-3: ours / Fig. 13 = 0.80-1.02 over its 6 points (adaptive and not, m = 3, 5, 7); p = 5e-4: ours / Fig. 13 = 0.63-1.13 over its 6 points (adaptive and not, m = 3, 5, 7). Fig. 13 thus behaves as a device-like model labelled by its two-qubit error, not as the stated uniform one (an inference from this match; the paper names no model for Fig. 13 and calls it the hardware's conditions). The adaptive gain (non-adaptive over adaptive error per Clifford): ours 1.24x (95 % 0.82-2.08) uniform, p = 1e-3, against the paper's 1.5x; 1.37x (95 % 1.19-1.59) uniform, p = 5e-4, against the paper's 1.8x; 1.22x (95 % 1.13-1.34) Helios-like, p = 1e-3, against the paper's 1.5x; 1.29x (95 % 0.93-2.16) Helios-like, p = 5e-4, against the paper's 1.8x; 1.19x (95 % 1.09-1.30) Helios-like decoded with pruning window 24, p = 1e-3, against the paper's 1.5x; 1.23x (95 % 1.17-1.30) Helios-like with the memory error per unit time doubled, p = 1e-3, against the paper's 1.5x. The paper gives its gains without an uncertainty; its Fig. 13 points carry 95 % error bars (digitized), and refitting them within those bars gives 1.47 (95 % 1.26-1.80) at p = 1e-3, 1.87 (95 % 1.30-4.31) at p = 5e-4: our Helios-like intervals overlap both, so the gains agree within the two uncertainties.
tqrb_distance_text: Complete TQRB sequences have lower fault distance: exactly 4 for 2 random sequences (m = 3; non-adaptive and along either adaptive branch, every logical class proven by exact integer programming) and at most 4-5 for 4 more (m = 3, 7; the integer program found an undetectable logical error of that weight and stopped after an hour without a matching lower bound) (`scripts/tqrb_distance.py`). In the sequence traced (`scripts/tqrb_lowweight.py`) the smallest undetectable error holds three faults of an outer check, whose hook errors the next automorphism and S0S1 carry, and one fault of the next inner check; the decoder's detectors are complete (with the observables they span every deterministic parity of the noiseless circuit, 1 sequence checked). The paper's distance-6 statement concerns one S0S1 followed by syndrome extraction, as checked above. Under the three natural cat assignments of the outer checks the same sequence has distance 4 (paired), 4 (shifted), 4 (xpair, used), so the assignment left open by Fig. 8 does not cause it.
gap_beam_text: Decoder dependence: the same shots (TQRB: 1e5 at p = 1.1e-3) decoded with other beam widths K and pruning windows Delta (states more than Delta nats below the best are dropped): K = 64, Delta = 12: failures 110, kept at γ = 4 37 (error at γ = 0 and 4: 0.85x and 1.83x the paper's; rejection at γ = 4 0.68x); K = 512, Delta = 12 (campaign): failures 106, kept at γ = 4 32 (error at γ = 0 and 4: 0.81x and 1.58x the paper's; rejection at γ = 4 0.70x); K = 512, Delta = 24: failures 86, kept at γ = 4 6 (error at γ = 0 and 4: 0.66x and 0.30x the paper's; rejection at γ = 4 0.86x). The paper's postselected TQRB values lie between our two pruning windows (at γ = 4 its error is 0.63x ours with Delta = 12 and 3.37x ours with Delta = 24, which also matches its rejection): forced-gap postselection is set by the decoder's pruning, and the paper does not publish its decoder settings. Without postselection the wider window lowers our error to 0.66x the paper's. Why: the campaign decoder makes some TQRB failures with an infinite gap, every state of the correct class pruned, and then never re-decodes them (re-decoding is triggered by a gap below 8 nats): at p = 0.0007, 15 of 36 failures in 100000 shots (minimal failing cores of 6 x 2, 5 x 3, 1 x 4, 2 x 5, 1 x 6 faults; exact most-likely-error decoding of the core is right in 11 and wrong in 4); at p = 0.0011, 26 of 107 failures in 100000 shots (minimal failing cores of 5 x 2, 12 x 3, 6 x 4, 1 x 5, 1 x 6, 1 x 7 faults; exact most-likely-error decoding of the core is right in 18 and wrong in 8). The pruning window, not the beam width, loses them.

chainmap_text: The paper's chain map is not published (its search method is arXiv:2607.02482); ours (`src/hase/chainmap.py`, `results/chainmap/F.json`) solves the chain-map conditions over GF(2) with at most two CNOTs per qubit by SAT: 30 CNOTs in two layers (depth 2, as the paper's), mapping the surface code's logical X onto C4-Helix's X_0, C4-Helix's Z_0 onto the surface code's logical Z and its Z_1 onto a surface stabilizer. Limits used (Carbon-Helix): 120 two-qubit gates and 145 ms per round (inner checks alone), 65 qubits (data plus one 4-qubit cat and one parity ancilla); error: the lowest of any configuration tried. uniform p = 0.001, Carbon-Helix ASE ambiguous, T=4 (B4): twoq 2.34x its limit, time 2.76x its limit, peak_qubits 1.42x its limit, eps_LQ 1.00x its limit (furthest: time_ms_per_round). uniform p = 0.001, Carbon-Helix ASE periodic, outer checks every 4 rounds (no escalation): twoq 2.05x its limit, time 2.42x its limit, peak_qubits 1.42x its limit, eps_LQ 1.84x its limit (furthest: time_ms_per_round). uniform p = 0.001, Carbon-Helix ASE periodic, outer checks every 16 rounds (no escalation): twoq 1.34x its limit, time 1.57x its limit, peak_qubits 1.42x its limit, eps_LQ 2.89x its limit (furthest: eps_LQ). uniform p = 0.001, Carbon-Helix ASE periodic, outer checks every 8 rounds (no escalation): twoq 1.58x its limit, time 1.85x its limit, peak_qubits 1.42x its limit, eps_LQ 1.89x its limit (furthest: eps_LQ). uniform p = 0.001, Carbon-Helix ASE periodic, outer checks every 8 rounds (no escalation, parallel weight-6): twoq 1.58x its limit, time 1.76x its limit, peak_qubits 1.48x its limit, eps_LQ 1.56x its limit (furthest: time_ms_per_round). Limits used (Carbon-Helix): 120 two-qubit gates and 145 ms per round (inner checks alone), 65 qubits (data plus one 4-qubit cat and one parity ancilla); error: the lowest of any configuration tried.

Push 1 (decoding cost and decoder error): primary beam K = 512 instead of 256, with staged re-decoding: 0.64 vs 0.58 s per shot at 14 faults per shot and 0.15 vs 0.11 s at 10, re-decodings 17 vs 37 per 200 shots, decisions unchanged on the benchmark sample (0 differ).

Push 2 (two-qubit gates, the criterion furthest from its limit after B4), uniform p = 1e-3: rotating outer checks R4 instead of a forced full measurement every 4 rounds: 236 vs 280 two-qubit gates and 479 vs 401 ms per round, error 1.9e-06 vs 5.5e-07 (extrapolated).

Push 2 (two-qubit gates, the criterion furthest from its limit after B4), Helios: rotating outer checks R4 instead of a forced full measurement every 4 rounds: 246 vs 285 two-qubit gates and 498 vs 413 ms per round, error 5.6e-06 vs 4.7e-06 (extrapolated).

Push 3 (time per round, the criterion furthest from its limit after R4), uniform p = 1e-3: one outer check per round (R8) instead of two: 370 vs 479 ms and 208 vs 236 two-qubit gates per round, error 1.2e-06 vs 1.9e-06 (extrapolated).

Push 4 (time per round, still the furthest), uniform p = 1e-3: weight-6 X and Z checks of a block measured in parallel when at most three blocks need them (R8F, peak 96 qubits): 349 vs 370 ms per round, error 9e-07 vs 1.2e-06 (extrapolated).

Push 3 (time per round, the criterion furthest from its limit after R4), Helios: one outer check per round (R8) instead of two: 387 vs 498 ms and 216 vs 246 two-qubit gates per round, error 3.7e-06 vs 5.6e-06 (extrapolated).

Push 4 (time per round, still the furthest), Helios: weight-6 X and Z checks of a block measured in parallel when at most three blocks need them (R8F, peak 96 qubits): 362 vs 387 ms per round, error 4.7e-06 vs 3.7e-06 (extrapolated).

Pushes 5 and 6 (time per round, still the furthest): one outer check every other round (R16F), then every fourth round (R32F), over 16 and 32 rounds (section 6, rotations over longer experiments).

Push 7 (time per round, the criterion furthest from its limit after R32F), Helios, 32 rounds: a block whose inner events are all of one type measures only its weight-6 checks of that type (R32FT): 230 vs 250 ms and 153 vs 172 two-qubit gates per round, peak 96 vs 96 qubits, error 1.5e-06 (95 % 1.5e-06-3.8e-06) vs 1.3e-06 (95 % 1.3e-06-3.6e-06) (extrapolated). Fewer escalations as well (0.063 against 0.101 full outer measurements per round): a block's unneeded checks no longer contribute measurement errors that make its change look ambiguous.

Next on time per round (evaluated): of R32FT's time per round the inner checks take 62 % (the limit), weight-6 checks after inner events 16 %, full outer measurements after escalations 9 % and the rotating outer checks 12 % (analysis/time_budget.py, direct path sampling at Helios's p). The weight-6 checks follow inner events, which locate the errors the inner code corrects, and escalations protect the ambiguous ones, so neither can be dropped; the rotating checks' layers hold 1-4 two-qubit gates, and packing them into the inner-check layers without changing any qubit's gate order saves at most 23 ms per check, 2.7 ms per round here (analysis/packing.py); halving the rotation rate again (one outer check every eighth round) would save at most half of the rotating checks' share, 6 % of the time per round, and needs 64-round experiments.

Push 8 (time per round, for the periodic rule - outer checks every 8 rounds, no escalation - which the interval study's windows made non-dominated at uniform p = 1e-3; its time and its error lie 1.85x and 1.89x from their limits, within 2 % of each other: push 8 took time, push 9 the error): outer checks every 16 rounds instead (16 rounds): 228 vs 268 ms and 161 vs 189 two-qubit gates per round, error 1.6e-06 (95 % 1.5e-06-1.8e-06) vs 1e-06 (95 % 1e-06-1.3e-06) (extrapolated): non-dominated, a success.

Push 9 (the error, after push 8 the criterion furthest from its limit for both periodic configurations: 1.89x, 2.89x): the weight-6 checks of a block measured with X and Z in parallel when at most three blocks need them (as R8F for the rotations), outer checks every 8 rounds: error 8.6e-07 (95 % 7.4e-07-1e-06) vs 1e-06 (95 % 1e-06-1.3e-06), 256 vs 268 ms and 189 vs 189 two-qubit gates per round, peak 96 vs 92 qubits (extrapolated): non-dominated, a success.

Next on time per round (evaluated, the periodic rule with parallel weight-6 checks, now its criterion furthest from its limit at 1.76x): the inner checks take 56 % (the limit), weight-6 checks after inner events 13 % and the periodic weight-6 and outer measurements 31 % (analysis/time_budget.py, direct path sampling at uniform p = 1e-3). A longer period trades error for time (push 8); measuring only the event's type of weight-6 checks, which saved 9 % of the rotations' time (push 7), would cut at most the event share, 13 % of the time per round here.
verdicts.failed:
- C4-Helix Helios memory: our central value 3e-05 is 0.65 of the paper's 4.6e-5 and its 95 % interval excludes 4.6e-5, while ours lies inside the paper's; the memory error per unit time is the unpublished input that moves it (x0.5: 1.6e-05, x2: 1.2e-04).
- TQRB shot-time savings: 21 %, 22 % against the paper's 23 % (hardware) and 24 % / 30 % (simulated at 1e-3 / 1e-4); the paper's time model is not published (gate-count-proportional time would give the 32-41 % gate savings).
- Decoder approximation (non-adaptive, uniform noise): 20 of 146 campaign failures are corrected by a 4x wider beam and a wider pruning window (K = 2048, Delta = 20; none of 306 sampled successes is broken by it); the confirmed-failure estimates of FINDINGS 2.5 count only the failures the stronger decoder also makes.
- Decoder approximation (B4, uniform noise): 18 of 123 campaign failures are corrected by a 4x wider beam and a wider pruning window (K = 2048, Delta = 20; none of 305 sampled successes is broken by it); the confirmed-failure estimates of FINDINGS 2.5 count only the failures the stronger decoder also makes.
- Decoder approximation (C, uniform noise): 22 of 169 campaign failures are corrected by a 4x wider beam and a wider pruning window (K = 2048, Delta = 20; none of 304 sampled successes is broken by it); the confirmed-failure estimates of FINDINGS 2.5 count only the failures the stronger decoder also makes.
- Decoder pruning window on the TQRB circuits (Frontier's documented K = 512, Delta = 12, used for every campaign): 15 of 36 failures at p = 0.0007; 26 of 107 failures at p = 0.0011 are made with an infinite gap - every state of the correct class pruned - on minimal cores of mostly 2-4 faults that exact decoding gets right in 11, 18 cases; a gap that large never triggers re-decoding, and Delta >= 18 decodes them (FINDINGS 1.7). On the same 1e5 shots at p = 1.1e-3, Delta = 24 leaves 86 of the 106 failures and 6 of the 32 kept at gamma = 4. They raise our TQRB error and survive forced-gap postselection; memory circuits are barely affected (the audit corrects 1-2 % of C4-Helix memory failures, FINDINGS 2.5).
- The first outer-check gadget (4-qubit cat, flags read only at the end; every result made with it is at commit 0ddbd72): two faults on one cat qubit, one before and one after its data CNOTs, leave up to four data errors and no flag, so the circuit's fault distance is 9 (an undetectable logical error found by exact integer programming over the end-of-circuit mechanisms), five faults can fail and the error falls as p^5 as p -> 0, not p^6. It was found after the first campaigns; the cat-parity gadget of FINDINGS 2.2 replaces it (end-of-circuit distance in FINDINGS 4) and every Carbon-Helix campaign was rerun with it.
- Fault distance of the whole Carbon-Helix circuit by generic solvers: integer programming over the whole two-round detector error model does not converge in 11 hours (X basis: best found 12, proven lower bound 4; Z basis: best found 11, proven lower bound 5), nor do CP-SAT, SCIP or CryptoMiniSat; the decomposition of FINDINGS 4 decides it instead: no undetected logical error of at most 10 faults in any of the 12 cases decided (each standing for all its schedules): the two-round non-adaptive circuit (bases X, Z, Z with the X checks last); non-adaptive extraction over the simulated 8 rounds after preparation (bases X, Z); every path of the escalating and periodic rules over 8 rounds (each weight-6 part optional, an outer-check part in every round) (basis X); every path of those rules over 4 rounds (the value comparisons' length) (bases X, Z); a periodic window of 16 rounds (push 8) (basis X); a periodic window of 8 rounds (basis X); two periodic windows of 4 rounds (basis X); four periodic windows of 2 rounds (basis X) - a fault distance of at least 11 on each; exactly 11 on the two-round non-adaptive circuit, Z basis (X checks last), where integer programming found an 11-fault logical error.
verdicts.open:
- Helios memory error per unit time during compiled extraction rounds (unpublished; the model uses the data-sheet depth-1 memory error spread over the published layer time). It sets the absolute error per round on Helios for both codes (FINDINGS 1.4 and section 8); settled by idle (Ramsey/echo) error of a data qubit measured across one compiled round.
- The noise model of the paper's Fig. 13 (not stated): Fig. 13 puts the non-adaptive benchmark 3.2-3.7x above the paper's own Fig. 12 under the stated uniform model, and our Helios-like model at the same two-qubit error reproduces it (FINDINGS 1.6). It decides only the comparison with Fig. 13, none of this work's results; settled by the model behind Fig. 13.
- The paper's shot-time model (per-operation durations on Helios; not published): its shot-time savings (23 % hardware, 24 % / 30 % simulated at 1e-3 / 1e-4) lie between ours with the Helios timing model (22 % / 26 %, m = 7) and time proportional to two-qubit gates (33 % / 40 %); it decides that comparison only; settled by the compiled durations.
- The paper's decoder settings (Frontier's beam and pruning window; not published): they decide the forced-gap postselection comparisons of Figs. 11 and 12 - Fig. 12's rejection and error lie between our pruning windows Delta = 12 and 24 on the same shots, and Fig. 11's high-threshold errors between ours with and without the failures that carry the pruning's signature, a gap of at least 31.5 nats (FINDINGS 1.7); none of this work's results depends on them (its campaigns use one stated configuration); settled by the paper's decoder configuration.
- Not a limit: the measurement/reset duration per batch on Helios (unpublished; 2 ms assumed). At 4 ms R4's time per round moves from 498 to 500 ms and C4-Helix / R4 from 8 to 8 (FINDINGS 8): it decides nothing here.
- Not a limit, for completeness: errors per round near 1e-8 at p ~ 5e-4 are beyond direct sampling (the problem statement's own obstacle); they come from stratified sampling and the polynomial model in the number of faults, labelled extrapolated, with their model range and the model's predictions of held-out strata (FINDINGS sections 3-4).
